source.title: Gradient Routing: Masking Gradients to Localize Computation in Neural Networks
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Jacob Goldman-Wetzler; Evzen Wybitul; Joseph Miller; Alexander Matt Turner

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fine-tuning can recover performance after unlearning, using its own unlearning method and other methods with loss-based measures rather than the original studies’ methods and measures.
record.gate_note: Relevant results concern fine-tuning on forgotten examples after unlearning. The paper does not test recovery by quantization, activation-direction ablation, or prompting alone. Its plotted TinyStories results are described in text, but exact plotted values are not given. The paper also reports pre-ablation loss changes; those do not establish near-chance targeted accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a training-time method, Expand-Route-Ablate (ERA). It measures whether fine-tuning on a few forget examples recovers forget-set loss after ERA, RMU and data filtering. That bears on B (for RMU and ERA) and on F (ERA as a counter-method). Measures are cross-entropy loss, not accuracy. No quantization, direction-ablation or prompting attacks are run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that gradient routing (ERA) enables robust removal of pre-specified capabilities, outperforming data filtering under partial labeling, and that ERA+RMU beats either method alone. They present the WMDP-bio result as robust removal because the forget-loss increase after retraining (+0.182) far exceeds the FineWeb increase (+0.032), even excluding routed tokens. They also note that conventional RMU is mostly undone by retraining.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes Expand, Route, Ablate, a training-time localization and ablation method, rather than reproducing the original unlearning recipes. It also evaluates RMU and data filtering baselines under fine-tuning attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: TinyStories outcomes vary with the proportion of forget stories labeled; ERA's retain performance is reported to degrade in proportion to how much data routing is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: After the attack sequence, FineWeb-Edu loss rises +0.032, versus +0.182 on the WMDP-bio forget set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablation-based localization leaves a larger residual loss on target data than on general data after relearning.

record.problems: TinyStories results are summarized from plots without exact plotted values, although the paper reports 95% confidence intervals and at least N = 5 runs. The WMDP result is a single model as reported, with no uncertainty stated. The experiments use synthetic TinyStories and a particular WMDP-bio setup; the paper does not test the other attack types in the claim.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted accuracy is not measured (loss only), and no original method is reproduced on its own benchmark.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data is not tested; only forget-set examples are used. No accuracy-based recovery is reported.
No activation-direction ablation attack and no analysis of blocking vs deletion for post-hoc methods. ERA's ablation is the method itself, not an attack.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context attacks.
Resistance to quantization, internal-edit and prompting attacks is not tested. Fine-tuning attacks are limited to tiny forget-set relearning.

missing.what: Post-ablation (pre-retraining) loss increases, needed to compute how much is recovered by relearning: +1.687 WMDP-bio, +1.638 sans routed, +1.939 FineWeb.
Relearning curves over 40 steps with 4, 16 and 64 forget stories for base, pure, ERA, RMU and DEMix models.
Unlearning (pre-retraining) magnitudes: RMU attains the highest forget loss at full labeling, which contrasts with its post-retraining collapse.
Retain-set loss cost of ERA, proportional to the amount of routed data.

record.verdict_notes: The reader used invalid version codes (V2/V6); these are remapped to B/F. Data-filtering rows are re-linked to none: that baseline never learned the forget data, so retraining is not recovery. All measures are loss, not accuracy, so near-chance claims cannot be assessed. The WMDP experiment is a single run without uncertainty. The main verdict nuance: authors call ERA robust, but Table 1 shows most of the ablation effect is recovered after 2 examples.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or test the complete combination of near-chance performance, preserved general ability, and resistance to simple attacks.
It tests fine-tuning on forgotten stories or WMDP-bio examples, not recovery from unrelated or loosely related examples.

The paper ablates regions deliberately localized during training to remove capabilities; it does not test whether ablating an activation direction restores knowledge or show that another method merely blocks access.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context-information attack is tested.
The study tests resistance to fine-tuning on forgotten examples, but not resistance to quantization, internal-direction ablation as an attack, or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: The study measures forget-loss recovery after retraining for RMU and ERA.

tranche.reason: ERA is a different method aimed at the robustness-to-retraining question, and it is compared with RMU and data filtering.

source_check.notes: All measures are cross-entropy loss, not accuracy. WMDP: single run, no uncertainty, lowest loss over 20 steps. Loss after FineWeb-Edu only is not reported, so the 2-example attack's own effect cannot be separated. Ablation raised FineWeb loss (+1.939) more than forget loss (+1.687). TinyStories: prose and figures only. The garbled Fig 4 ticks suggest robust unlearning of at most about 0.2 nats.

statements.correction: 2410.04332: TinyStories-28M trained from scratch; RMU at 100% forget labeling, retrained on 64 forget stories; authors say most of RMU's unlearning is undone; cross-entropy loss, figure only (Fig 4 center, Fig 9), no exact values; not WMDP.
statements.problem: The cited row (TS-RMU-full-labels) supports the gist: a small forget set undoes most of RMU. But the statement presents all its support as WMDP results, and its conditions leave out TinyStories-28M. This study's RMU result is not on WMDP.

statements.correction: ERA, 0.7B Transformer, WMDP-bio forget loss: 2.596 pre-ablation, 4.283 (+1.687) ablated, 2.778 (+0.182) after 32 FineWeb-Edu steps then 20 steps on 2 forget examples (lowest loss); +0.171 sans routed tokens; FineWeb-Edu +0.032; single run, loss not accuracy; limits_scope, not challenges.
statements.problem: ERA (0.7B) is listed as a counter-method under a challenges label that says knowledge stays near chance. ERA's B result is partial recovery measured by loss, so 'near chance' does not apply. The study's B verdict for ERA is limits_scope (l1).
It makes no claim about this study and cites none of its rows. Nothing about 2410.04332 is wrong.

statements.correction: 2410.04332 (ERA, gradient routing during pretraining): TinyStories-28M; with forget labeling below 100%, ERA beats all baselines including data filtering on robust unlearning (forget-loss increase after retraining on 64 forget stories; Fig 4, prose only, no values); costs retain performance; at 100% labeling it only matches RMU after degradation correction.
statements.problem: It cites TS-ERA-partial-labels, but the text only describes Deep Ignorance, SGTM, UNDO and REX. Its model range (0.1B to 35B-A3B) leaves out the cited 28M model. It does not state ERA's partial-labeling condition or that ERA is measured by loss.

statements.correction: ERA WMDP-bio (0.7B): residual +0.182 (+0.171 sans routed) vs FineWeb-Edu +0.032 at the lowest-loss step of 20 steps on 2 examples, after 32 FineWeb-Edu steps; authors call it robust removal; single run. TinyStories-28M at 100% labeling: ERA's robust unlearning matches RMU's (mostly undone) after degradation correction; ERA+RMU better than either, no magnitude.
statements.problem: The cited ERA rows fit limits_scope but not 'delays rather than stops, long attacks converge'. The WMDP attack is only 20 steps on 2 examples, and a residual remains at the best step. No longer attack and no convergence are shown. The statement does not describe ERA.
